newsitem.title: UK: Europe not a big issue for British voters -poll.
newsitem.headline: Europe not a big issue for British voters -poll.

text.p: Europe is far from being a vital issue for British voters, and the planned European single currency is less of a worry than inflation, according to a poll to be published on Tuesday in the Mirror newspaper.

Britain's Conservative government is frequently in conflict with its European Union partners and the ruling party is deeply divided over the single currency, but the poll conducted by ICM suggests the average Briton is much more relaxed about the EU.

Europe came last in a list of nine election issues that voters were asked to comment on. Only 32 percent of respondents said it was very important to them, compared with 90 percent who cited the National Health Service and 85 percent education.

The single currency came sixth out of seven financial issues. Only 37 percent said they were very worried about it, against 53 percent who were concerned about the price of food. Meanwhile, 38 percent of people wanted Britain to play a bigger role in Europe, twice as many as wanted the government to pull out altogether.
The Mirror, which generally supports the opposition Labour party, said in an editorial that its poll showed the electorate would not be fooled by the Conservatives' "euro scare".
"What is incredible about the poll's findings is that it comes after the most sustained, one-sided, blatant campaign of propaganda against Europe," it said.
ICM interviewed 750 people between February 18 and 20.
